subject: AcreetionOS Update — July 17, 2026
body:
Our continuous integration pipeline has just been improved with the addition of per-pipeline staging directories to avoid publish races between concurrent builds, and relative symlinks for the latest.iso file, making our ISO build process more reliable. This enhancement is a direct result of our community's efforts to refine and stabilize our workflow, ensuring that our users receive the most up-to-date and stable versions of AcreetionOS, which can be found on our website at https://acreetionos.org/.

Development
The recent updates to our continuous integration pipeline have been a significant focus for our community, with the goal of creating a more streamlined and efficient build process. As an Arch-based distribution, we rely on the Arch repos and tooling like pacman to manage packages, and our improved pipeline will help us better leverage these resources. You can learn more about our development process and how to get involved on our wiki at https://acreetionos.org/wiki.html.

Community
The AcreetionOS community has been actively engaged in discussions around the latest Emacs 31.1 release, which brings a number of exciting changes, including the removal of the old Emacs Lisp compiler. Our community is always looking for ways to improve and contribute to the project, and you can join the conversation on our website or by checking out our documentation at https://acreetionos.org/docs.html. For the latest news and updates, be sure to check out our changelog at https://acreetionos.org/changelog.html or flash updates at https://acreetionos.org/flash.html.
